elements.name: Parent User
elements.rationale: Role checks across backend and frontend show the system explicitly recognizes and serves parent users as a distinct actor.

elements.name: Child User
elements.rationale: Role checks show the application distinguishes child users and exposes child-specific behavior and access paths.

elements.name: Administrator
elements.rationale: Admin-only role checks demonstrate a separate administrator actor outside the modeled backend processes.

elements.name: Authentication Service
elements.rationale: The auth router is mounted as a coherent backend service handling registration, login, identity lookup, and password change with reads and writes to user and child profile data.

elements.name: Child Profile Service
elements.rationale: The children router is mounted as one coherent process that manages child profiles, approvals, and history while reading and writing child profile and video records.

elements.name: Video Management Service
elements.rationale: The videos router is mounted as a single service for upload, listing, retrieval, streaming-related access, and interaction operations on video data.

elements.name: User Profile and Administration Service
elements.rationale: The users router is mounted as a coherent process for profile access, profile update, statistics, and admin management over user, child-profile, and video data.

elements.name: Age Check Middleware
elements.rationale: A dedicated middleware component reads user records by id, indicating a separate processing step used to enforce age-related logic.
elements.uncertainty_note: Only database read facts are available for this middleware; its exact invocation points are not present in the provided facts.

elements.name: Frontend Web Application
elements.rationale: Frontend API bindings and HTTP client configuration show a browser-based application process that calls backend services over HTTP.

elements.name: User Database
elements.rationale: The User mongoose model maps to the users MongoDB collection, and multiple routes read from and write to that collection.

elements.name: Child Profiles Database
elements.rationale: The ChildProfile model maps to the childprofiles collection, which is used persistently for child records, approvals, and histories.

elements.name: Video Database
elements.rationale: The Video model maps to the videos collection, with routes performing persistent reads, counts, aggregates, and writes on video records.

elements.name: Uploaded Image Files
elements.rationale: Multer disk storage and directory creation facts show profile and ID images are written to a filesystem location for persistent storage.

elements.name: Uploaded Video Files
elements.rationale: Video uploads are written to a backend uploads directory that is also exposed via static serving, indicating a persistent file store for uploaded media.

elements.name: Browser Local Storage
elements.rationale: Frontend code reads and writes tokens, user objects, and banner state in localStorage, making browser local storage a persistent client-side data store.
